title: Symptoms
subtitle: A noble cause may call for sacrifice; vengeance demands it.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Gutsy move. But are you sure about this, kid?

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Besides, how do we know your device hasn't already triggered? If we inject more of that stuff into you, even an antidote might not be enough.

items.speaker: X
items.text: It's the best solution I can see. Given I only became polymerized earlier today, I should be especially sensitive to a polymer-based poison. My reaction will be easiest to observe in small, controlled doses.

items.speaker: X
items.text: It's what Madam Lucy would do.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: No, it isn't. She would never approve of such an irresponsible act of self-sacrifice. Nor will I.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Let's just hope that Vertin can convince Maxim to give up an antidote.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I won't allow you to gamble your life on this while there is still a chance to find the solution another way.
Their argument has drawn the attention of the still-sane scientists.

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: Sorry, miss. But I think your colleague is right. Dangerous as his plan is, we don't have time to wait. Every minute that passes, more of us could be exposed.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Ugh. This is exactly what I was afraid of, X. Your irresponsible nature is practically infectious.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: You just had to drag this whole world down with that special brand of arcanist madness.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Hold on, Mesmer. I didn't set off this chain of events. Call me a mad scientist if you like, but I don't deserve the blame for what's happening here.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I don't care who's to blame. I still won't let you do this to yourself.

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: This isn't the time to argue, kids. Maybe you're infecting me with "arcane madness," or maybe the poison already got to my head. Doesn't matter.

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: I'll do it. I'll be your guinea pig.

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: Besides, I've put myself through regular trials of intoxication for most of my life. What's another neurotoxin?

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Eh, that's not the point!

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: No. It's not. The point is that I'm not letting a kid put himself on the line on my account.

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: My vision's starting to get blurry. Good bet I'm already exposed. So, let's get on with it.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Ugh. If that's the case, we may as well try. But I'm not happy with it.

items.speaker: Scientist VI
items.text: Alright, nice and tight.
After confirming that Ethan is securely tied, Mesmer Jr. takes out an injector that she brought from Laplace. Using a familiar tool makes her feel a little more at ease.

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: Hey, kid. You don't have to do this yourself if you don't agree. It's a simple injection.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Shush. I'm the only other person here with medical experience.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I would never have allowed anyone to do this back home. I guess I'm the mad scientist now.
Mesmer Jr. stabs the needle into Ethan's arm, pushing the plunger down in a slow, even release.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Hm. Your body temperature is rising, likely a reaction to the toxin or the antidote.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: How do you feel?

items.speaker: Ethan Brown
items.text: My limbs are numb, and my eyes are losing focus. Feels like I'm staring up at the northern lights.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: First antidote, not working. We'll observe you over the next five minutes and then try the next one.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Mesmer ...

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: What now? We're doing what you wanted, aren't we? Just leave me to my work.
Mesmer Jr. tries not to lose her temper as she looks back at X.

items.speaker: X
items.text: The antidotes could react to each other if applied on the same subject, so why not try the next one on me?

items.speaker: X
items.text: It's about time. I'm beginning to experience symptoms: diplopia, nausea, the works.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: You'd better come back with a solution, Vertin.
The Belyash that crashed through the ceiling is now lying on the ruins it created.

items.speaker: Right
items.text: Combat concluded. No signs of injury or damage. We should return to our mission, comrades.
It's at this moment that she notices a slight inconsistency between the Twins' movements.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Left? Are you alright?

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Running diagnostic.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Are you hurt?

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Negative. Test complete. All systems functioning. We can proceed.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: The breach in the ceiling will allow us to compensate for lost time.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Transport mode activated.
Left sweeps her companion into her arms again, preparing to jump up from the Belyash's remains.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Again, please brace for impact.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Not to worry. I feel quite safe in your arms.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: I am pleased to hear that, Comrade Doctor.
Left nods at her companion. She then jumps nimbly through the hole in the ceiling to reach the second floor.
The warning lights flash as the airtight door creaks open, illuminating the power control room.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Please be careful, comrade. We advise you to stay outside of the room until it is secured.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Hah. That must be why Sechenov always preferred the company of robots—always ready to sacrifice themselves for the good of humanity.
Maxim sits relaxedly in a soft chair in front of the instrument panel.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: I wonder what you really think. Do you see other robots as your "people"?

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Does that emotion module of yours prick with doubt or pain when you see your kind die?

items.speaker: Left
items.text: We are not obligated to answer your questions, Maxim.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Oh, I suppose the real question is, can a robot truly even die? *sigh* That's a question that would have fascinated me when I was younger.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Maxim, what did you do to the THOUGHT Devices?

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: What makes you think I would tell you?
Maxim stands up, fixing his wrinkled trousers.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm not from here. I don't know what Kollektiv 2.0 means to you or to this country. I just want to understand.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You expressed concerns about it before. Maybe you think the world would be better off without it. I don't know, but what I do know is that what you've done here is wrong.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Whatever the intention was, it wasn't worth killing innocent people.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: "Whatever the intention," hmph, you're more right than you know, young lady.
A huge robot with a round belly appears behind Maxim.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: But I'm not special—making ends justify the means—that's just the way we do things here. Haven't you figured that out?
The robot is torn apart, its components scattering all over the floor. Sparks pop from its torn wiring, lighting Maxim's dispirited face.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Target down. Area secured.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Please, Maxim, tell us, is there an antidote or at least some way to prevent exposure?

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Is that your best effort? Heheh. The Argentum Unit would have at least brought truth serum.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: If you were trying to stop Kollektiv 2.0 from launching, you already succeeded. There's no way they'll release it on schedule after everything that happened here.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Do more people really need to die just to make this a bigger scandal?
Maxim places one hand on his temple, pondering, then lets it fall to his side.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Sechenov deserves every punishment coming to him, but you're right. I never wanted people to suffer in vain.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: There is an antidote.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Abnormal heart rhythm detected. Comrade Doctor, be careful. He may be engaging in deception.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's alright.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Please, Maxim. Just share it with us.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: It's a simple antidote. Though I'm afraid I'll be taking the first dose.
He draws a pistol out of his pocket.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: One shot of lead to end the suffering of a hopeless man in this hopeless country!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Maxim! No!
